body: The maintainer decided on 2026-11-23: this issue is not on the v0.26.0 cut list. It goes under Known issues of v0.26.0. The fix ships in the next minor.

Addition from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23). His words: "you would never helix on a outside cut.. as you dont need to "lead in" like that.. so an outside cut would default to a ARC or straight approach in the plane of its cut, starting outside the stock boundary with a given value."

The expected behaviour, in addition to the body:
- An Outside cut never uses a helix entry, and it does not use a ramp entry.
- The tool goes down to the cut level outside the stock boundary, in air.
- The default approach is an arc or a straight line, in the plane of the cut.
- The approach starts outside the stock boundary by a given distance. That distance is a parameter with a default value.
- A pinning test checks that an Outside pass has no helix move and no ramp move into material, and that each entry starts outside the stock boundary.

Addition from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23, seen in the simulation). His words: "Simulation show that the path approach breaks down, instead of "going around the" object in the plane, it "lifts over" it picking up the contour ont he other side and starts ramping down back and forth to the desired depth again.. Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

Seen in the simulation:
- The pass does not go around the part in the plane of the cut.
- The tool lifts over the part.
- It starts the contour again on the other side.
- It then ramps down back and forth to the cut depth again.

Expected:
- Each ring goes around the part in the plane of the cut and stays at depth.
- The tool does not lift between the parts of one ring.
- Where a ring is split (for example at the neck of the part, or against the stock edge), the link stays in the plane when the path is clear. A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason.
- A pinning test counts the lifts and the re-entries on one level of an Outside pass. On a part without a split ring, the test expects no lift and no re-entry.

Addition from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23), about the Lead in / Lead out page. His words: "when selecting outside - the leadin/leadout type Helix,Ramp,Plunge - gets unselectable And only Arc is the available option. The arc atm, is showing as a "straight" plunge down.. which is fine for transporting to the plane, but it should happen outside the stock box. - and also we see no movement of a an arc to wal into the wall of the stockbox - so no viable approach is getting generated using the Arc approach. The Arc Sweep and Arc Radius inpputs does nothing to affect the approach"

Seen:
- With Pass starts at = Outside, the Lead in / Lead out page disables Helix, Ramp and Plunge. Only Arc is available. This part is correct.
- But the generated entry is a straight plunge down. The plunge is not outside the stock box: it comes down on the stock edge.
- There is no arc move from outside into the wall of the stock box.
- A change of Arc sweep or Arc radius does not change the approach.
- Thus the Arc entry that the page offers is not generated for an Outside pass.

Expected:
- The plunge to the cut plane happens outside the stock box, in air, by the approach distance.
- Then an arc lead-in in the cut plane (Arc sweep, Arc radius) moves the tool into the stock wall and onto the first ring.
- Arc sweep and Arc radius change the generated arc.
- Pins: (1) the plunge XY is outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance; (2) the first cutting move after the plunge is an arc in the cut plane; (3) a change of Arc radius changes that arc's radius in the output.

Addition from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23), about "Pass starts at = Inside". His words: "picking "inside" makes perfect rings, but the cutter planges straight down into the material.. instead of starting outside the stock box"

Seen:
- With Pass starts at = Inside, the rings are correct.
- But the tool plunges straight down into material at the start of the pass.

Expected:
- The tool does not plunge straight down into material.
- The entry starts outside the stock box, in air, as for Outside.

The research must cover this case too. It must say if Inside and Outside share the entry code. It must also say if one fix covers both, or if Inside needs its own sub-issue. A pin checks that no entry of an Inside pass is a straight plunge into material.

Addition from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23), about "Pass starts at = Inside". His words: "And it also does a shit ton of uncessary lifts.." Seen: the Inside pass also lifts the tool many times without need. Expected: the same rule as for Outside. Each ring stays at depth and links in the plane. A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture, and the status line names the reason. The lift-count pin covers Inside and Outside.

Design rule from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23). His words: "The only thing that differs and inside and outsided strategy is actually where the tool starts.. inside the bounding box, or outsided the bounding box. Why there is different cut strategies between outside, inside and auto (which is insane) is strange.."

The rule:
- Inside, Outside and Auto use one ring planner, one linking rule and one entry rule.
- "Pass starts at" changes only the start point of the tool: inside the bounding box, or outside the bounding box.
- Auto only selects one of the two start points. It does not select a different cut strategy.
- A pin checks that Inside and Outside on the same part give the same set of rings, and that only the start point and the ring order differ.

The research must find where the three choices go into different code paths. It must file the unification as a P1 sub-issue, and the other sub-issues must build on it.

Three screenshots from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-23). They show the same part, tool and settings with each "Pass starts at" value, on build v0.26.0 `f729592f0`. The screenshots are not attached, because they show a private model. The facts that they show:

**Inside**: 2876 moves, 17 plunges at 300, 1184 arcs, 1 level, **414 warnings**.
- `warning: feed moves 873 and 1044 cross in XY at shared depth - repeated on 413 more moves (to 2860)`. The feed moves of this pass cross each other at the same depth.
- `warning: Pass start Inside: the inner edge of this area is the part wall, so each level starts with a cut of the full tool width along the part`.
- The rings look correct, but the entry plunges into material (see the earlier comment).

**Outside**: 3551 moves, 8 plunges, 194 arcs, 1 warning.
- `Entry: the arc's lead room is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead at (323.399, 116.110) - fix: a smaller helix radius (or a minimum radius), a pre-drilled start hole, or a smaller tool`.
- This explains the straight plunge: the Arc entry falls back to an axial dive. The lead room check finds the arc blocked, although the start is at the stock edge. An Outside start must have room in air outside the stock box. The fix suggestions (helix, start hole) do not apply to an Outside pass.
- The paths in the neck areas are short linear moves, not rings.

**Auto**: 4901 moves, 2 plunges, 581 arcs, 0 warnings.
- The maintainer's words: "auto planner is not even rings anymore..".
- Rings in the neck areas, but zigzag or raster-like moves in the long side areas. Auto does not pick one of the two start points of the same ring set. It makes a different pattern.

Questions for the research:
1. Does the crossing of feed moves at shared depth on Inside (414 warnings) cut material twice or gouge? Do these warnings block the post? If not, say why. (Prime Directive: a result that a check finds unsafe must block the post.)
2. Why does the lead room check find no room for the Outside arc, at a start that should be in air outside the stock box?
3. Which code makes the Auto pattern, and why is it not the Inside or Outside ring set?

See also #3743 (the review of all 2D ring planners).

## Research result 1 of 2: where each behaviour is made, and when it started

All paths are on `origin/main` at `6167d30af`.

### Repro (throwaway test, not committed)

- Part: a dog-bone outline. Two discs of R 12 at x = +-15, joined by a neck 8 mm wide. Part size 54 x 24 mm.
- Stock box: 80 x 50 mm, centred on the part. The machining region is the box grown by the tool radius, with the part as the hole (as an Outside containment makes it).
- Tool D8. Stepover 2 mm. One level, Z 0 to Z -6. 2D Offset strategy `Waterline`, climb. `Links::PLANAR` (the 2D Offset default).
- Generator: `machining2d::pocket_started(..., PassStart::X)`, the call of the 2D Offset op (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:851-857`, strategy at `:1067`).

Readings on `main` (`6167d30af`), Arc entry, Arc radius 4, Arc sweep 90:

| Pass starts at | floor runs | runs that end on the part wall | lifts | re-entries | ramp moves | plunges | first dive: tool centre outside the box |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outside | 14 | 14 | 14 | 13 | 366 | 1 | -0.50 mm (inside the box) |
| Inside | 8 | 0 | 8 | 7 | 0 | 8 | -9.00 mm (in solid stock) |
| Auto | 7 | 1 | 7 | 6 | 423 | 3 | -4.00 mm (in solid stock) |

- Arc radius 4 -> 10 and Arc sweep 90 -> 45: the Outside path does not change. The Inside and Auto paths change.
- `Link::KeepDown` as the pass link: Outside still has 14 lifts. Inside goes from 8 to 7 lifts.
- With a Plunge entry, Outside has 14 plunges on `47aa341ff^1`. With a Helix entry, the first dive is a helix 2.76 mm inside the box.
- No pair of floor feeds crossed in XY on this part, with any start (see result 2, question 1).

### Bisect

| Commit | Outside, Arc entry | Outside, Plunge entry |
|---|---|---|
| `e313aa663` (#3353, Pass starts at added) | 14 lifts, 13 re-entries, 292 ramp moves (vertical arc chords), 12 plunges | 14 lifts, 13 re-entries, 14 plunges |
| `47aa341ff^1` (before #3577) | same as `e313aa663` | same |
| `6167d30af` (`main`) | 14 lifts, 13 re-entries, 366 ramp moves, 1 plunge | 14 lifts, 13 re-entries, 366 ramp moves, 1 plunge |

- The 14 ring pieces that end on the part wall, the 14 lifts and the plunge on the stock edge started with #3353. They are not a regression of #3577.
- #3577 changed only the 13 re-entries. They were plunges or helices into stock. Now they are the zig-zag ramp along the pass (`level_ramp_entry::dead_end_ramp`). This is the "ramped cuts ... back and forth" that the maintainer saw.
- #3620 cannot change the path. It changes only `crates/sim/src/verify`. `git diff 37aca7f8c^1 47aa341ff^1 -- crates/motion crates/cl` is empty.

### Where each behaviour is made

1. **Three different ring sets.** "Pass starts at" selects a different ring planner, not only a start point.
   - Dispatch: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs:101-120` (`ring_plan_ramped`). Auto goes to `plan_passes` (`:120`). Inside and Outside go to `level_pieces` + `level_order::order` (`:102-106`). Outside and Inside fall back to the Auto set on a leftover (`:107-118`).
   - Auto: `pocket_plan.rs:20-36` -> `waterscan.rs:62` `waterline_passes`. It offsets the whole cutter-centre area from both edges and chains the loops. In a long, narrow side band the loops collapse to thin back-and-forth loops. This is the "zigzag or raster-like" pattern (inferred from the code; not measured on the private model).
   - Outside: `level_rings.rs:188-203`. The rings are offsets of the OUTER edge only (`filled.offset(-j*step)`), cut by the cutter-centre area (`curves`). They are parallel to the stock box, not to the part. The part cuts each ring into open pieces that end on the part wall. Repro: 14 of 14 runs end on the part wall. This is "not following the contour of the selection".
   - Inside: `level_rings.rs:169-187`. The rings are offsets of the holes (the part), grown out. They are parallel to the part. Repro: 0 runs end on the part wall.
   - More switches on the start side: `pocket.rs:308-347` (`cleared_links: side.start != Auto` at `:346`, `ramp_starts` at `:347`), `pocket_avoid.rs:147, 209-210`, `pocket_hsm_start.rs:42-63` (Adaptive: Outside gets the stock, Inside and Auto do not), `pocket_hsm.rs:61-62, 92-100`, `level_order.rs:143-145` (dead-end marks for Outside only), `generate.rs:982, 1102` (the stock band goes to the plan only when the start is not Auto).
2. **The entry selection** (one code path for Auto, Inside and Outside): `ladder_links.rs:55-92` (`descend`) -> `descent.rs:120-149` (`plan`, `plan_core`) -> `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`). The entry is always placed at the first point of the first pass (`l.pass.first()`, `:217`). For Outside that point is on the stock edge. There is no air approach outside the stock box, and no approach distance.
3. **Where the Arc lead-in becomes a straight plunge.**
   - The `Arc` entry is a VERTICAL-plane arc onto the first cut (`entry.rs:37-41`, `descent.rs:262-277`). It is not an in-plane lead-in.
   - Its lead chord is proved against the cutter-centre area: `|s, q| l.cen.chord_ok(s, q)` (`descent.rs:271`). For Outside the cutter-centre area ends at the stock box. The air outside the box is not in it. Thus `entry_arc.rs:146-152` halves the radius to its floor and returns "the arc's lead room is blocked".
   - Then `descent_dive.rs:169-187` (`substituted_dive`) posts "axial dive on the floor instead" at the pass start. That is the straight plunge on the stock edge.
   - The horizontal (G17) arc entry, `arc_xy` (`descent_xy.rs:205-220`), is skipped when the arm is `Arc` (`:218-219`). It also proves only inside the legal area.
   - Thus Arc radius and Arc sweep cannot change an Outside entry.
4. **Ring-to-ring linking and the lift decision.**
   - `ladder_links.rs:154-225` (`pass_link`). The 2D Offset uses `Links::PLANAR` (`links.rs:86-94`; `crates/app/src/operation/types/links.rs:65-67`), whose pass link is `Link::Retract`. `Retract` lifts at EVERY pass break, with no proof and no reason (`:161-163`, `:182`).
   - `KeepDown` stays down only when `link_proof` (`:243-261`) passes: the chord is in the cutter-centre area and crosses no planned cut. For a start side, `cleared_links` also asks that the chord runs through material already cut (`through_cut`, `:230-237`). A link between two Outside pieces that end on the part wall crosses the part, so it always lifts.
   - The planner joins pieces only when `linkable` within reach (`level_order.rs:110-151`). Each other piece is a new pass, thus a lift.
   - After a lift, the re-entry is the dead-end ramp (`ladder_links.rs:188-191`) or the solid restart of #2265 (`:200-211`, helix or ramp into stock).
5. **The dead-end ramp of #3577.** `level_ramp_entry.rs:100-127` (`dead_end_ramp`), marks at `level_order.rs:143-145`, plan check `level_rings.rs:108`, call at `ladder_links.rs:188-191`. Decision: `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md`.

Result 2 of 2 answers the questions of the latest comment and lists the sub-issues.

## Research result 2 of 2: the questions of the latest comment, and the sub-issues

### 1. Inside: do the 414 "cross in XY at shared depth" warnings cut twice or gouge? Do they block the post?

- The text is the Display of `Warning::Crossing` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs:467-471`). The verifier makes it in `crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs:56-61`: two feed moves at the same depth cross in XY.
- It is a path law, not a gouge check. The two moves stay in the cutter-centre area, so the second move cuts the same place again. The gouge and collision checks are separate.
- It blocks the post. `Warning::blocks_post` (`types.rs:441-448`) is true for each kind except Scallop, ProbeSearch, SinkerFinishOrder, DrillUndersize, StrategyFallback and FluteShort. Crossing is not in that list. Thus the Prime Directive holds, and no separate "unsafe result passes" sub-issue is necessary.
- The synthetic dog-bone part gave 0 crossings with each start. The crossings come from the Inside planner on the private model. #3744 makes one ring set and has the pin `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing` on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step`.

### 2. Why does the lead room check find no room for the Outside arc?

- The `Arc` entry is a vertical-plane arc. Its lead chord is proved against the cutter-centre area (`descent.rs:271`, `entry_arc.rs:146-152`).
- For Outside, the cutter-centre area ends at the stock box. The air outside the box is not part of it. Thus no Arc lead fits, and `descent_dive.rs:169-187` posts "axial dive on the floor instead" at the pass start, on the stock edge. Repro: the tool centre is 0.50 mm inside the box.
- The fix text (helix radius, start hole) is the generic text of `substituted_dive`. It does not apply to a start side.
- The fix is #3746: an air entry outside the box by the approach distance (#3745), then a G17 arc lead in the cut plane.

### 3. Which code makes the Auto pattern?

- Auto calls `plan_passes` (`level_rings.rs:120`) -> `waterline_passes` (`pocket_plan.rs:32-33`, `waterscan.rs:62`). It offsets the whole cutter-centre area from the two edges (the stock box and the part) and chains the loops.
- In a long narrow side band, the offsets of the two edges meet. The loops become thin and collapse, and the chain goes back and forth. This gives the "zigzag or raster-like" look. (Inferred from the code; the private model was not opened.)
- Inside uses offsets of the part (`level_rings.rs:169-187`). Outside uses offsets of the stock box (`level_rings.rs:188-203`). Thus the three choices give three ring sets. #3744 makes them one set.

### Inside and the entry code

Inside and Outside share the entry code (`ladder_links.rs:55-92` -> `descent.rs:120-286`). One fix covers the two: #3746 has the Inside pin "no entry of an Inside pass is a straight plunge into material". The Inside lifts have the same cause as the Outside lifts (the `Retract` pass link of `Links::PLANAR`), so #3747 covers Inside and Outside with one lift-count pin.

Related: #3743 (the review of all 2D ring planners; #3744 is its 2D Offset slice) and #3423 (P7, lifts between pieces; #3747 covers it).

Each part of this issue is covered by a sub-issue. This umbrella closes now, by the `needs-research` procedure.

Research done. Each part of this issue is covered by a sub-issue: #3744 (one ring set), #3745 (approach distance), #3746 (air entry and arc lead-in, Inside included), #3747 (in-plane links, Inside included), #3748 (no helix or ramp; retire the #3577 dead-end ramp).
